page.layout: One page of text in a single column; no margin notes; running head at top with page number at top left; a catchword-free page with a signature-free foot; a short line "Vt" at lower right is a catchword.

main_text.p: Tenacitas eft, per quam fubftantia mixti fit lenta, & tenaciter cohærens.
Illius fcilicet, quod multo humido aqueo, cū ficco terreo fubtiliore probè permixto, ac lento calore cocto, eft præditum.
Ratione tenacitatis mixtum aliquando fit tractile, ut trahendo in partes longas latasq; extendi posfit: aliquando ductile, ut istu violento in longum latumq; diduci queat.
Prefsilitas eft, per quam corpus mixtum prefsum in feipsum fe arctius colligere potest.
Cujus nempe fubstantia ratione humidi, cum ficco cocti ac uniti, est porofa.
Idq; vel per impressionem certam quandam formam recipiendo : vel per condensationem crafsius fiendo.
Siccitatis autem respectu mixto inest Humectilitas: vis admittendi imbibendiq; humorem, in mixto, quod copioso ficco terreo, porofo, atque humore destituto, pollet.
main_text.head: Atque hæ qualitates mixti constitutionem respiciunt.
main_text.p: Ad ejusdem dissolutionem pertinent, quæ vel mixti partium disjunctionem, vel totalem illius destructionem inducendi vim habent.
Prioris generis sunt, tum fractilitas & friabilitas; tum fectilitas & fissilitas.
Fractilitas est, per quam in majores & inæquales partes mixtum frangi potest.

page.notes: Scan is a 17th-century Latin text; headings "Atque hæ qualitates..." set in italic and treated as level 2 heading. Long s rendered as s; "Tractile" and "Ductile" read as tractile/ductile from italic print, moderately certain. Running head read as "DE QVALITATIBVS MIXTI" (printed in small capitals with the page number 18 at left). The "Vt" at lower right is the catchword for the next page and is recorded in bottom_margin.
